Vocational education is available to students at the secondary and [tertiary](/wiki/Tertiary_education "Tertiary education") level.[[507]](#cite_note-Ministry_of_Edu_China-2022-530) More than 10 million Chinese students graduated from vocational colleges every year.[[508]](#cite_note-531) In 2024, about 92.0 percent of students continued their education at a three-year senior secondary school, while 60.8 percent of secondary school graduates were enrolled in higher education.[[509]](#cite_note-auto-532)

Under chief justices Jay, Rutledge, and [Ellsworth](/wiki/Oliver_Ellsworth "Oliver Ellsworth") (1789–1801), the court heard few cases; its first decision was *[West v. Barnes](/wiki/West_v._Barnes "West v. Barnes")* (1791), a case involving procedure.[[17]](#cite_note-17) As the court initially had only six members, every decision that it made by a majority was also made by two-thirds (voting four to two).[[18]](#cite_note-18) However, Congress has always allowed less than the court's full membership to make decisions, starting with a [quorum](/wiki/Quorum "Quorum") of four justices in 1789.[[19]](#cite_note-19) The court lacked a home of its own and had little prestige,[[20]](#cite_note-tws31oct01-20) a situation not helped by the era's highest-profile case, *[Chisholm v. Georgia](/wiki/Chisholm_v._Georgia "Chisholm v. Georgia")* (1793), which was reversed within two years by the adoption of the [Eleventh Amendment](/wiki/Eleventh_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution "Eleventh Amendment to the United States Constitution").[[21]](#cite_note-21)

The Yas Marina Circuit was designed by [Hermann Tilke](/wiki/Hermann_Tilke "Hermann Tilke") and is located on [Yas Island](/wiki/Yas_Island "Yas Island") – a 2,550 hectares (25.5 km2) island on the east coast of [Abu Dhabi](/wiki/Abu_Dhabi "Abu Dhabi"). The [2009 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix](/wiki/2009_Abu_Dhabi_Grand_Prix "2009 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix") was the first major event to take place on the circuit.[[42]](#cite_note-AbuDhabi-42)

In June 2021, Saif Al Noaimi, acting CEO of Abu Dhabi Motorsports Management, announced that modifications to the track's Grand Prix layout had been approved, with the modifications being completed in time for the [2021 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix](/wiki/2021_Abu_Dhabi_Grand_Prix "2021 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix").[[43]](#cite_note-43) The turn 5–6 chicane and turn 7 hairpin were replaced by a single, widened hairpin, now turn 5; the triple chicane and 90 degree left hander at turns 11–14 were replaced by a single, sweeping banked curve, now turn 9; and the radiuses of turns 17–19 (now 12–14), and the penultimate turn 20 (now 15), were widened to allow cars to carry more speed through the third sector.[[44]](#cite_note-44)[[45]](#cite_note-45)

As a senior in 2004, he won the [Doak Walker Award](/wiki/Doak_Walker_Award "Doak Walker Award") as the nation's top running back and was recognized as a first-team [All-American](/wiki/College_Football_All-America_Team "College Football All-America Team"). He finished his college career with 5,540 rushing yards to rank tenth all-time in [NCAA](/wiki/NCAA "NCAA") [Division I-A](/wiki/Division_I-A "Division I-A") history, and second only to [Ricky Williams](/wiki/Ricky_Williams "Ricky Williams") in Longhorns team history.

He was often compared to Williams because of similarities in running style, college choice suspensions,[[2]](#cite_note-2)[[3]](#cite_note-3) appearance (roughly the same size and build in college, and both with [dreadlocks](/wiki/Dreadlocks "Dreadlocks") early in their careers) and the fact that they had both been minor-league baseball players.

While at Texas, Benson majored in [social work](/wiki/Social_work "Social work") and [sociology](/wiki/Sociology "Sociology"). He was included on the Texas athletics directors' academic honor roll and the [Big 12](/wiki/Big_12 "Big 12") commissioner's honor roll in Fall 2003. While in college, Benson was arrested twice, once for possession of marijuana and the other for [trespassing](/wiki/Trespass_to_land "Trespass to land"). The marijuana case was dropped after a friend claimed responsibility. Benson was sentenced to eight days in jail for the trespassing conviction, but he spent no time in prison because of overcrowding at the [Travis County Jail](/wiki/Travis_County_Corrections_Bureau "Travis County Corrections Bureau"). Though his father owned a small tea trading business in Taizhou, the family was relatively poor. His mother was a teacher and died when he was 7, and he was raised by an aunt. Hu's father was denounced during the [Cultural Revolution](/wiki/Cultural_Revolution "Cultural Revolution"), an event that (together with his relatively humble origins) apparently had a deep effect upon Hu, who diligently tried to clear his father's name.[[3]](#cite_note-5)

He joined the [Chinese Communist Party](/wiki/Chinese_Communist_Party "Chinese Communist Party") (CCP) in April 1964. The [1954 Italian expedition](/wiki/1954_Italian_expedition_to_K2 "1954 Italian expedition to K2") finally succeeded in ascending to the summit of K2 via the Abruzzi Spur on 31 July 1954. The expedition was led by [Ardito Desio](/wiki/Ardito_Desio "Ardito Desio"), and the two climbers who reached the summit were [Lino Lacedelli](/wiki/Lino_Lacedelli "Lino Lacedelli") and [Achille Compagnoni](/wiki/Achille_Compagnoni "Achille Compagnoni"). The team included a Pakistani member, Colonel Muhammad Ata-ullah, who had been a part of the 1953 American expedition. Also on the expedition were [Walter Bonatti](/wiki/Walter_Bonatti "Walter Bonatti") and Pakistani Hunza porter [Amir Mehdi](/wiki/Amir_Mehdi "Amir Mehdi"), who both proved vital to the expedition's success in that they carried [oxygen tanks](/wiki/Oxygen_tank "Oxygen tank") to 8,100 metres (26,600 ft) for Lacedelli and Compagnoni. The [ascent is controversial](/wiki/1954_Italian_Karakoram_expedition_controversy "1954 Italian Karakoram expedition controversy") because Lacedelli and Compagnoni established their camp at a higher elevation than originally agreed with Mehdi and Bonatti. It being too dark to ascend or descend, Mehdi and Bonatti were forced to overnight without shelter above 8,000 metres (26,000 ft), leaving the oxygen tanks behind as requested when they descended. Bonatti and Mehdi survived, but Mehdi was hospitalised for months and had to have his toes amputated because of frostbite. Microsoft and Gates launched their first retail version of [Microsoft Windows](/wiki/Microsoft_Windows "Microsoft Windows") on November 20, 1985, in an attempt to fend off competition from [Apple](/wiki/Apple_Inc. "Apple Inc.")'s [Macintosh](/wiki/Classic_Mac_OS "Classic Mac OS") [GUI](/wiki/GUI "GUI"), which had captivated consumers with its simplicity and ease of use.[[47]](#cite_note-ahmwbi-48) In August 1986, the company struck a deal with [IBM](/wiki/IBM "IBM") to develop a separate operating system called [OS/2](/wiki/OS/2 "OS/2"). Although the two companies successfully developed the first version of the new system, the partnership deteriorated due to mounting creative differences.[[48]](#cite_note-49) The operating system [grew out of DOS](/wiki/Windows_9x#Windows_prior_to_95 "Windows 9x") in an organic fashion over a decade until [Windows 95](/wiki/Windows_95 "Windows 95"), which hid the DOS prompt by default. [Windows XP](/wiki/Windows_XP "Windows XP") was released one year after Gates stepped down as Microsoft CEO.[[49]](#cite_note-cnettop-50) [Windows 8.1](/wiki/Windows_8.1 "Windows 8.1") was the last version of the OS released before Gates left the chair of the firm to [John W. Thompson](/wiki/John_W._Thompson "John W. Thompson") on February 5, 2014.[[50]](#cite_note-chairex-51)

Jupiter :: Gravitational domain and influence :: Moons :: Galilean moons :: chunk_0018
Main article: [Galilean moons](/wiki/Galilean_moons "Galilean moons")

The moons discovered by Galileo—Io, Europa, Ganymede, and Callisto—are among the largest in the Solar System. The orbits of Io, Europa, and Ganymede form a pattern known as a [Laplace resonance](/wiki/Laplace_resonance "Laplace resonance"); for every four orbits that Io makes around Jupiter, Europa makes exactly two orbits and Ganymede makes exactly one. This resonance causes the gravitational effects of the three large moons to distort their orbits into elliptical shapes, because each moon receives an extra tug from its neighbours at the same point in every orbit it makes. The [tidal force](/wiki/Tidal_force "Tidal force") from Jupiter, on the other hand, works to [circularize](/wiki/Tidal_circularization "Tidal circularization") their orbits.[[148]](#cite_note-154)

The [eccentricity](/wiki/Orbital_eccentricity "Orbital eccentricity") of their orbits causes regular flexing of the three moons' shapes, with Jupiter's gravity stretching them out as they approach it and allowing them to spring back to more spherical shapes as they swing away. The [friction](/wiki/Friction "Friction") created by this tidal flexing [generates heat](/wiki/Tidal_acceleration#Tidal_heating "Tidal acceleration") in the interior of the moons.[[149]](#cite_note-Eccen304-155) This is seen most dramatically in the [volcanic activity](/wiki/Io_(moon)#Volcanism "Io (moon)") of Io (which is subject to the strongest tidal forces),[[149]](#cite_note-Eccen304-155) and to a lesser degree in the geological youth of [Europa's surface](/wiki/Europa_(moon)#Surface_features "Europa (moon)"), which indicates recent resurfacing of the moon's exterior.[[150]](#cite_note-156)
